clue.text: Primarily suppress flatulence? The French do

definitions.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of suppress is used

parts.note: flatulence is wind in the gut
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek question about stifling wind, with a wry note that the French do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' at the end looks like a verb finishing the sentence about the French, but it is the definition, in its slang sense of cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech to do someone is to cheat or con them out of something.

clue.text: Weird sisters pollarding birches, say

indicators.note: pollarding a tree cuts off its top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a birch is a bundle of twigs used for flogging, an example of switches

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of strange women lopping the crowns off birch trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weird Sisters are the three witches in Shakespeare's Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare names the three witches in Macbeth the Weird Sisters.

clue.text: Nearly time to crash?

parts.note: nigh means near or nearly
to crash is to fall heavily

explanation.surface: Someone yawning that it is almost bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also defines: when darkness comes it is almost time to crash, in the slang sense of going to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is when people start thinking of bed, and crash is slang for going to sleep.

clue.text: Tempt one lad to stray

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off course, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A seducer luring a young man away from the straight and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stray' rearranges the letters of ONE LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to entice or encourage them misleadingly, a phrasal synonym of tempt.

clue.text: Story of Dracula, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: Dracula is a count, a nobleman by title

explanation.surface: Looks like a reference to Bram Stoker's tale of the vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story of Dracula' reads as one phrase, but 'of' is only a link; Dracula is 'a count', which spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrative report of events, a synonym of story.

clue.text: Sort of office layout extremely unusual in a wine store

indicators.note: in places the outside letters inside the store word

parts.note: a cellar is where wine is kept

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of unusual

explanation.surface: An odd open-plan office crammed into a wine vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes U and L from 'unusual', and 'in' sets them inside CELLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellular office is divided into separate small rooms, the opposite of open-plan.

clue.text: Sex appeal? A ton, when topless

indicators.note: topless removes the top character, here the leading figure one

parts.note: a ton is slang for 100 miles per hour, written 100 MPH, with the figures read as letters

explanation.surface: A cheeky line linking speed, sex appeal and going topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A ton' is 100 mph; 'when topless' drops the 1, leaving 00MPH, which reads as the answer with the zeros as Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vitality or sexual attractiveness.

clue.text: Cry in support of kid's mother that's not big city material

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece in support of another sits beneath it
that's not means without, so the big city letters are removed

parts.note: a kid is a young goat, whose mother is a nanny goat
NY is New York, the Big Apple
to keen is to wail in grief

explanation.surface: A child's mother wailing about some fabric that isn't from the metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: The kid is a young goat, so its mother is a NANNY; take away NY, then put KEEN underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing, so it is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Wee condoms, perhaps, if emerging from Spooner's boxers

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: widdle is a childish word for wee
Mates is a British brand of condoms

explanation.surface: A smutty image of tiny contraceptives falling out of someone's underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: Mates is a British condom brand. Swapping the W and M sounds of WIDDLE MATES gives the answer by sound. 'boxers' is fighters, not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Middleweights are boxers in a mid-range weight division.

clue.text: Mark's tense opening letter from Crete

indicators.note: opening means the tense letter cuts into the Greek letter

parts.note: sigma is a Greek letter, and Crete is Greek
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a Mark's nervous first letter sent from a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' passes as a man's name; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, or a physical mark on the body.

clue.text: Light up with Scottish smoker during one row

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: during means the chimney word sits within the row word

parts.note: a line is a row
lum is Scots for a chimney, which smokes

explanation.surface: A Scottish smoker lighting up while sitting in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' looks like a person, but it is a chimney: LUM in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: To illumine is a literary word for to light up or illuminate.

clue.text: Adult with two 14s around?

indicators.note: around puts the two letters either side of the adult letter
two calls for the daughter abbreviation to appear twice

parts.note: 14 across is daughter, abbreviated D
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up with a couple of daughters in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an adult surrounded by two daughters is a father.
explanation.definitionFit: A father of two girls is an adult with daughters around him.

clue.text: Playing together with no hesitation in Jewish quarter

indicators.note: playing about with letters rearranges them
with no means the hesitation sound is taken away

parts.note: er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Children playing together without pause in a Jewish neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes ER from TOGETHER, leaving TOGETH, which 'Playing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a ghetto was the quarter of a city where Jews were made to live.

clue.text: Issue raised by the Guardian, not the Scotsman, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the leftover letters come out in an unexpected order
not removes the Scotsman's letters from the newspaper name

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A child brought up reading the Guardian rather than the Scotsman, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the Scotsman' drops IAN from THEGUARDIAN; 'surprisingly' rearranges THEGUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, and a girl child is one kind of offspring.

clue.text: One of three patriarchs from two different 5s

parts.note: two different kinds of account are named: ISA, an Individual Savings Account
5 across is account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: A puzzle-style remark that a biblical patriarch comes from two kinds of account.
explanation.walkthrough: ISA is a British tax-free savings account; AC is the usual abbreviation for account.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are the three patriarchs of Israel in Genesis.

clue.text: Smearing teacher, having deployed a bug outside home

parts.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters wrap around the home word
deployed means spread out, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A teacher accused of planting a listening device around someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges A BUG into AUBG, which 'outside' wraps round IN. 'bug' looks like a spy device but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear something all over, so bedaubing is smearing.

clue.text: Fine and dandy before return match you lost

indicators.note: before puts the dandy word first in the down entry

parts.note: a beau is a dandy, a fashionable man

indicators.note: return means the match word is read backwards

parts.note: to fit is to match
U sounds like you in text speak
L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports tables

explanation.surface: A cheerful report that you lost the return match, said to be fine and dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses FIT into TIF. 'Fine and dandy' looks like one phrase, but only 'Fine' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine can mean handsome or lovely, as in a fine sight, a synonym of lovely-looking.

clue.text: Slight hill some say is a monster

indicators.note: some say means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: minor means slight and a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Someone claiming a small hill is actually a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur is the bull-headed monster of Greek myth kept in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: Apparently nobody's 12's brother died keeping goal

indicators.note: keeping means the outer letters hold the goal word

parts.note: 12 across is dad, and a dad's brother is an uncle
aim means goal

explanation.surface: A father's brother who died while holding on to a goal no one wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts AIM inside UNCLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nobody has asked to have back seems to belong to no one, that is, it is not claimed.

clue.text: 12 embraces partners getting married — a regular occurrence

indicators.note: embraces means the twelve word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: twelve o'clock in the day is noon
East and West are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: Seems to describe midday weddings as a frequent event.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' here is just the number, not clue 12. EW are bridge partners East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar phase when the moon shows no light recurs every month or so, a regular event.

clue.text: Crazy about hotel swimming pool location

indicators.note: about means the crazy word goes around the hotel letter

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone raving about where the hotel pool is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it puts BATS around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Public baths are a British name for municipal swimming pools.

clue.text: Killer game

definitions.meaning: a word-guessing game played with pencil and paper

explanation.surface: Two words that seem to call a game deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: An executioner by hanging bears this title, and so does the classic letter-guessing paper game.

clue.text: City can get on top of old Mexican in New York?

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting on top of means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A city overpowering an old Mexican living in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this is only one example: a Mexican in the US is called a Latino.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a Latino is someone of Latin American origin, which a Mexican living there would be.

clue.text: Final appearance of US actress — good!

parts.note: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood star of Sunset Boulevard

explanation.surface: A cheer for an American actress's last performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloria Swanson starred in Sunset Boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's last show is named after the legendary dying song of the bird.

clue.text: Turning water green

indicators.note: turning round means the brand name is read backwards

parts.note: Evian is a brand of bottled mineral water

explanation.surface: Water going green, as a pond might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like a colour, but it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or gullible, a synonym of innocent and unworldly.

clue.text: Tip from Antonio Conte about start of play

indicators.note: a tip is the end point, here the opening letter of Antonio
about means the letters of Conte are turned around in a new order

explanation.surface: Football advice from the Italian manager Antonio Conte about how to start a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CONTE into CTONE. Antonio Conte is an Italian football manager, which sends minds to kick-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The first act is how a stage play begins.

clue.text: Somewhat posh? A topper, perhaps

indicators.note: somewhat means part of, so a few letters are drawn from inside the words

explanation.surface: Asks whether a top hat is a little upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'posH A Topper', and the whole clue also describes the answer: a topper is one and is rather posh.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat, or topper, is one kind of headwear, and it tends to look smart.

clue.text: So controlling!

definitions.meaning: the fifth note of the scale, soh in sol-fa

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about someone bossy.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the fifth degree of a scale, soh, has this name; the word also means commanding or in control.

clue.text: Trendy female confronts a setter's notoriety

indicators.note: confronts means standing in front of, so the earlier pieces come first

parts.note: in means fashionable
my is what the setter would say for their own

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman facing up to a crossword setter's bad reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is the compiler, so 'setter's' is MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is a bad reputation, being well known for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Running nude not dead hard? Not tried yet

indicators.note: running here means mixing, so the letters are rearranged
not tells us to remove the dead letter

explanation.surface: A streaker who is apparently not dead hard, yet not tried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not dead' drops D from NUDE, and 'Running' rearranges NUE with HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case that has not been heard has not been tried by a judge.

clue.text: Sounding very windy, if one that'll fly through stormy night shortly

indicators.note: through puts the bird inside the scrambled letters
stormy means turbulent, so the letters are tossed about
shortly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: an owl is a bird that flies through the night

explanation.surface: A gale-force night with something flying through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the last letter, 'stormy' turns the remaining NIGH into HING, and 'through' sets the bird inside. 'Sounding' looks like a homophone signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A howling wind makes a loud wailing noise, the sound of a gale.
